summary: Consolidate fragmented SaaS licenses into single identity-scoped allocations and implement recurring seat-reconciliation
description:
Issue summary:
We have ~15 distinct vendor tenant allocations across multiple products (Figma, Sentry, Lucidchart, Miro and a few smaller eval accounts) that are not tied to standardized identity groups. This has led to unused seats, duplicate purchases, and manual provisioning overhead when teams change.

Impact:
- Estimated wasted spend: ~10% of license budget for Q1 2026 (~$18k).
- Slow onboarding (average 3-5 business days) for cross-functional contractors because provisioning paths vary by product.
- Increased audit risk: no single canonical mapping of seats to manager/owner for 6 vendors.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
1) Run a one-time consolidation: move eligible users to identity-scoped seat pools using SCIM/OIDC for Figma, Miro, Lucidchart and Sentry where supported.
2) Decommission 3 smaller eval tenants and reassign remaining active users into consolidated tenants.
3) Create a recurring monthly seat-reconciliation job (owner: IT Procurement) that outputs a CSV + variance report and opens an automated INT ticket when variance > 5%.
4) Attach a Finance budget code and standardize PO flow for renewals; prepare a one-page procurement playbook for RD and Product managers.

Timeline:
- Week 1 (Mar 9–13): complete inventory & stakeholder approvals.
- Week 2–3 (Mar 16–27): perform migrations in low-risk windows; run smoke tests.
- Week 4 (Mar 30–Apr 3): enable monthly reconciliation automation and handover to Procurement.

Budget / Approvals:
Estimated one-time engineering/IT effort ~ 40 hours. Procurement to confirm whether vendor bulk discount renegotiation can offset migration overhead.

Notes:
Do not proceed with forced user removals without manager approval; use phased communication and a 7-day reclamation window for inactive seats.
